<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

  /* Reading mode hides the chrome and the empty .arxiv-html-header marker: the pinned JS reads
     the marker's display to know which way to toggle. The marker draws no box. */
  .arxiv-html-header { display: contents; }
  html[data-reading-mode="enabled"] :is(.arxiv-html-site-chrome, .arxiv-html-header, .ds-site-footer) { display: none; }
  /* The paper controls' icons are blocks, so they sit centred (the pinned JS shows the theme
     icon by making its span a block). */
  .arxiv-html-site-chrome .ds-site-header-tools svg { display: block; width: 18px; height: 18px; flex-shrink: 0; fill: currentColor; }
  /* ar5iv dims every image in dark mode and puts it on a white wash, for paper figures;
     arXiv's own render as they are (the logo on the bar, the funder logos on their white
     chips). Important: ar5iv's dark rules are unlayered, as specific as
     :root:not([data-theme]) img:not(.ltx_no_dark_filter). */
  :is(.ds-site-header, .ds-site-footer) img { filter: none !important; }
  .ds-site-header img { background-color: transparent !important; }

  /* Wide (the theme's 1280px): the theme lays the body out as a grid whose full-width top rows
     were the band's and its sticky reader bar's. The band takes the first and scrolls away; the
     header, the paper's bar (no site navigation, the paper's controls), takes the second and
     stays in view, the one sticky bar, with the anchor clearance that requires (DESIGN-POLICIES).
     The controls show their names. */
  @media (min-width: 1280px) {
    html { scroll-padding-top: 80px; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome { display: contents; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome > #ds-announcement { grid-area: announce; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome > .ds-site-header { grid-area: header; position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 3; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-icon { display: none; }
  }
  /* Narrow: the header scrolls away, and the controls show icons (names kept for screen
     readers; Why HTML? goes). The theme's contents panel is fixed below where its old sticky
     bar was, and hidden only once the reader has closed it, so until then it is an invisible box
     over the header and the paper: it shows only while open, under the chrome, in its place in
     the page. The paper's footer (build logs, reporting instructions) keeps the text's side
     inset; the theme gives it none, so it met the screen edges. */
  @media (max-width: 1279px) {
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-wide { display: none; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-label { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0 0 0 0); white-space: nowrap; }
    html:not([data-toc-display="block"]) .ltx_page_navbar { display: none; }
    .ltx_page_navbar { position: absolute; top: auto; }
    .arxiv-html-footer { padding-inline: 1rem; }
  }

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">We present EmbeddingGemma 2, an open multimodal embedding model which natively represents text, images, audio, video, and combinations thereof in a unified space. Our approach introduces improvements such as simplified per-layer embeddings and a multi-stage curriculum with modality and objective progression which ensure strong quality across unimodal, cross-modal, and mixed-modal evaluations. Notably, in comprehensive embedding benchmarks across all modalities, EmbeddingGemma 2 establishes a new Pareto frontier, outperforming both specialist models and models two to twelve times larger. Furthermore, our design offers flexibility for resource-constrained environments, supporting selective modality encoder loading, adjustable vision token budgets, truncatable embedding dimensions, and quantized weights. We present ablations analyzing key decisions and release EmbeddingGemma 2 to promote further research.</p>
  
</div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Embedding models map data to fixed-length vector representations, placing semantically similar data near each other in the embedding space. Text embedding models have become a popular choice for tasks like information retrieval, semantic similarity, clustering, and retrieval-augmented generation. However, to work with audio and visual data, these require additional tools like automatic speech recognition (ASR) and image captioners which both add computational cost and fail to capture signals like fine-grained visual details and non-verbal or environmental sounds.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Multimodal embedding models like CLIP <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">1</a>]</cite>, ALIGN <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>]</cite>, and SigLIP <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">3</a>]</cite> add a modality tower for vision, and so achieve strong cross-modal quality, but they are unable to natively process mixed-modal input to capture interactions between input modalities. Recent efforts have adapted Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) into embedding models that allow interleaved mixed-modal input and support more complex tasks such as visual question answering and visual grounding <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>, <a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">5</a>, <a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>, <a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>]</cite>; subsequent work has built on more capable MLLMs to incorporate video and audio modalities <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>, <a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>, <a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>, <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>, <a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>]</cite>. However, as MLLMs have grown in size, so have embedding models adapted from them. These models typically contain several billion parameters, making them prohibitively expensive for applications that are latency-sensitive, high-throughput, or require on-device deployment for privacy or offline access.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">In this paper, we introduce EmbeddingGemma 2,<span id="footnote1" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">1</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">1</sup>
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">1</span>
            
            
            
            
            
            
            
          Our model is available at <a href="https://ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/embeddinggemma" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/embeddinggemma</a>.</span></span></span> a 744M-parameter general-purpose multimodal embedding model that maps text, images, video, and audio—as well as arbitrary interleaved combinations thereof—into a single unified embedding space (<a href="#S1.F1" title="In 1 Introduction ‣ EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>). EmbeddingGemma 2 combines a 271M-parameter bidirectional transformer backbone (embedder included) with a 167M-parameter vision encoder and a 305M-parameter audio encoder. The modality encoders independently convert media into sequences of soft token embeddings that enter the shared transformer backbone, which means these parameters are modular: EmbeddingGemma 2 can alternatively be run with 271M parameters as a text-only model, with 439M as a vision-language model, or with 577M as an audio-language model.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S1.F1" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2610.37364v1/diagram.png" id="S1.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:357/299;" width="357" height="299" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S1.F1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 1</span>: </span><span id="S1.F1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">EmbeddingGemma 2 natively maps text, images, video, audio, and combinations thereof into a unified, semantically-aligned vector space.
</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The model builds on the architecture and weights from the capable Gemma 4 model family <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">13</a>]</cite> and learns from the powerful Gemini Embedding 2 model <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>]</cite>. Our training regime consists of three stages spanning various tasks, modalities, and domains, which results in a broadly capable model, excelling at problems like code search, visual question answering, video moment retrieval, audio classification, and much more. We separate text-only and multimodal training as a form of curriculum learning, and separate distillation from contrastive and regularization objectives in order to effectively learn an embedding space tailored to the model. For extreme resource-constrained settings, the model offers high-quality truncated embeddings and separate checkpoints adapted with quantization-aware training.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">We present ablation studies explaining our architectural and training choices. We find that simplifying per-layer embeddings to omit the dedicated lookup table not only reduces cost but improves performance; we present the effects of using different vision token budgets during training and inference, observing it only significantly affects tasks like document retrieval which require fine-grained visual understanding; we demonstrate the importance of co-training the vision encoder; we show the impact of finetuning with contrastive learning rather than distillation; and we confirm the value of native audio understanding over ASR.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S1.F2" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.37364v1/frontiers.svg" id="S1.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/309;" width="476" height="309"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S1.F2.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 2</span>: </span><span id="S1.F2.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
EmbeddingGemma 2 establishes a new Pareto frontier across benchmarks covering code, image, video, visual documents, and audio. Methods and detailed results in <a href="#S4" title="4 Evaluation ‣ EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>.
<br class="ltx_break"><sup id="S1.F2.5.1" class="ltx_sup">∗</sup>Mean(Task) for MTEB(Code), MAEB, and MMEB-v2; Mean(Type) for MIEB(lite).
</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Finally, we evaluate the model on seven major, comprehensive benchmark suites spanning text, code, image, video, document, speech, and sound inputs. EmbeddingGemma 2 establishes a new Pareto frontier across benchmarks spanning all modalities (<a href="#S1.F2" title="In 1 Introduction ‣ EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>). Despite using fewer parameters for text than its predecessor and handling more modalities, it improves on both multilingual text and code benchmarks. On multimodal evals, EmbeddingGemma 2 often matches or exceeds the quality of specialized and multi-billion-parameter models.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>EmbeddingGemma 2</h2>

<section id="S2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.1 </span>Architecture</h3>

<section id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Backbone</h4>

<div id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The backbone follows a transformer architecture <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">14</a>]</cite> with bidirectional attention. Given a tokenized input sequence <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐓</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{T}</annotation></semantics></math> of length <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math>, we map discrete text tokens via an embedder <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{E}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{E}</annotation></semantics></math> into input token embeddings <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{T}_{\text{in}}=\mathcal{E}(\mathbf{T})\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times d_{M}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐓</mi><mtext>in</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐓</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>M</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{T}_{\text{in}}=\mathcal{E}(\mathbf{T})\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times d_{M}}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{M}</annotation></semantics></math> is the model dimension used for the transformer’s inner representations (note multimodal inputs are incorporated into <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{T}_{\text{in}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐓</mi><mtext>in</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{T}_{\text{in}}</annotation></semantics></math> as well, described in detail in <a href="#S2.SS2" title="2.2 Input ‣ 2 EmbeddingGemma 2 ‣ EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a>). We then apply <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{n}</annotation></semantics></math>, an <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>-layer transformer with bidirectional attention, to produce a sequence of output token embeddings <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{T}_{\text{out}}=\mathcal{M}_{n}(\mathbf{T}_{\text{in}})\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times d_{M}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐓</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐓</mi><mtext>in</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>M</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{T}_{\text{out}}=\mathcal{M}_{n}(\mathbf{T}_{\text{in}})\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times d_{M}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Next, we employ mean pooling <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}</annotation></semantics></math> to average the output token embeddings along the sequence axis to generate a single embedding representing all the information in the input, producing <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{P}_{\text{embed}}=\mathcal{P}(\mathbf{T}_{\text{out}})\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{M}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐏</mi><mtext>embed</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐓</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>M</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{P}_{\text{embed}}=\mathcal{P}(\mathbf{T}_{\text{out}})\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{M}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Finally, we apply a randomly initialized linear projection <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> to scale the embedding to the target dimension <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>, followed by <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>-normalization to produce the final unit-norm embedding, <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{E}=\frac{f(\mathbf{P}_{\text{embed}})}{\|f(\mathbf{P}_{\text{embed}})\|_{2}}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐄</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐏</mi><mtext>embed</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐏</mi><mtext>embed</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mfrac><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{E}=\frac{f(\mathbf{P}_{\text{embed}})}{\|f(\mathbf{P}_{\text{embed}})\|_{2}}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math>. In EmbeddingGemma 2, we use <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=24,d_{M}=512,d=768" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>24</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>512</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>768</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=24,d_{M}=512,d=768</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Notably, the transformer <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{n}</annotation></semantics></math> harnesses per-layer embeddings (PLE), as introduced in Gemma 3n <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">15</a>]</cite>. These act as residual inputs which give each layer a path to receive tailored information directly from the input token embeddings. However, instead of additionally utilizing a large, separate token lookup table specifically for PLE, EmbeddingGemma 2 simply adapts the input embeddings <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{T}_{\text{in}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐓</mi><mtext>in</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{T}_{\text{in}}</annotation></semantics></math> produced by the main embedding table and modality encoders (comparison in <a href="#S3.T2" title="In 3.1 Per-Layer Embeddings Table ‣ 3 Ablation Studies ‣ EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>). For each layer <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l\in[n]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l\in[n]</annotation></semantics></math>, we project the input token embeddings into a layer-specific representation <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{P}_{l}=\text{RMSNorm}(p_{l}(\mathbf{T}_{\text{in}}))\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times d_{P}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐏</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext>RMSNorm</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐓</mi><mtext>in</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>P</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{P}_{l}=\text{RMSNorm}(p_{l}(\mathbf{T}_{\text{in}}))\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times d_{P}}</annotation></semantics></math> via linear projection <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{l}</annotation></semantics></math>. We use the layer’s output <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{H}^{\prime}_{l}\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times d_{M}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐇</mi><mi>l</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>M</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{H}^{\prime}_{l}\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times d_{M}}</annotation></semantics></math> to compute gate <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{G}_{l}=\sigma(g_{l}(\mathbf{H}^{\prime}_{l}))\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times d_{P}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐆</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐇</mi><mi>l</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>P</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{G}_{l}=\sigma(g_{l}(\mathbf{H}^{\prime}_{l}))\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times d_{P}}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{l}</annotation></semantics></math> is a linear projection and <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> is a GELU activation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">16</a>]</cite>. We then modulate the per-layer input and project it back to the model dimension via linear projection <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{l}</annotation></semantics></math>, producing update <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{U}_{l}=\text{RMSNorm}(u_{l}(\mathbf{G}_{l}\odot\mathbf{P}_{l}))\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times d_{M}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐔</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext>RMSNorm</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐆</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⊙</mo><msub><mi>𝐏</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>M</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{U}_{l}=\text{RMSNorm}(u_{l}(\mathbf{G}_{l}\odot\mathbf{P}_{l}))\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times d_{M}}</annotation></semantics></math>, to finally yield <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{H}_{l}=\mathbf{H}^{\prime}_{l}+\mathbf{U}_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐇</mi><mi>l</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>𝐔</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{H}_{l}=\mathbf{H}^{\prime}_{l}+\mathbf{U}_{l}</annotation></semantics></math> to be processed by the next layer. In EmbeddingGemma 2, we use <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{P}=d_{M}=512" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>P</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>512</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{P}=d_{M}=512</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Modality Encoders</h4>

<div id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As in Gemma 4, the vision encoder is a vision transformer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">17</a>, ViT,]</cite> with a patch size of 16 and the audio encoder consists of two downsampling convolution layers followed by twelve conformer layers <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>]</cite>, based on the Universal Speech Model (USM) architecture <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">19</a>]</cite>. The vision and audio encoders produce soft tokens with dimensionalities <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{V}=768" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>V</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>768</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{V}=768</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{A}=1536" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1536</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{A}=1536</annotation></semantics></math>, respectively. Using learned linear projections <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi_{\text{vis}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mtext>vis</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{\text{vis}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi_{\text{aud}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mtext>aud</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{\text{aud}}</annotation></semantics></math>, we map these to the model dimension <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{d_{M}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{d_{M}}</annotation></semantics></math>. These soft tokens are interleaved with the token embeddings at their corresponding positions to form a combined input token embedding sequence <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{T}_{\text{in}}\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times d_{M}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐓</mi><mtext>in</mtext></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>M</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{T}_{\text{in}}\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times d_{M}}</annotation></semantics></math>, which is processed as described above. See <a href="#S2.SS2" title="2.2 Input ‣ 2 EmbeddingGemma 2 ‣ EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a> below for more details on how multimodal inputs are handled.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.2 </span>Input</h3>

<div id="S2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In general, an input <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> consists of an ordered sequence of <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math> modality segments <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x=(s_{1},s_{2},\dots,s_{M})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x=(s_{1},s_{2},\dots,s_{M})</annotation></semantics></math>, where each segment <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{m}</annotation></semantics></math> belongs to one of four modalities:</p>
<ol id="S2.I1" class="ltx_enumerate ltx_leftmargin_flush">
<li id="S2.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S2.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Text</span> is tokenized into <math id="S2.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{\text{txt}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mtext>txt</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{\text{txt}}</annotation></semantics></math> tokens which are mapped via the embedding table to a sequence of token embeddings: <math id="S2.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{T}_{\text{txt}}=\mathcal{E}(s_{m})\in\mathbb{R}^{N_{\text{txt}}\times d_{M}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐓</mi><mtext>txt</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mtext>txt</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>M</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{T}_{\text{txt}}=\mathcal{E}(s_{m})\in\mathbb{R}^{N_{\text{txt}}\times d_{M}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S2.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;padding-top:5.0pt;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S2.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Images</span> are each processed by the vision encoder <math id="S2.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{V}</annotation></semantics></math> and spatially pooled to below a fixed budget of <math id="S2.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{\text{vis}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mtext>vis</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{\text{vis}}</annotation></semantics></math> soft tokens, <math id="S2.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{T}^{\prime}_{\text{vis}}=\mathcal{V}(s_{m})\in\mathbb{R}^{N_{\text{vis}}\times d_{V}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐓</mi><mtext>vis</mtext><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mtext>vis</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>V</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{T}^{\prime}_{\text{vis}}=\mathcal{V}(s_{m})\in\mathbb{R}^{N_{\text{vis}}\times d_{V}}</annotation></semantics></math>. <math id="S2.I1.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{\text{vis}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mtext>vis</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{\text{vis}}</annotation></semantics></math> defaults to <math id="S2.I1.i2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="280" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>280</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">280</annotation></semantics></math> for images and <math id="S2.I1.i2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="140" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>140</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">140</annotation></semantics></math> for video during training, but is configurable to <math id="S2.I1.i2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="70" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>70</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">70</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S2.I1.i2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="140" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>140</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">140</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S2.I1.i2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="280" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>280</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">280</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S2.I1.i2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="560" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>560</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">560</annotation></semantics></math>, or <math id="S2.I1.i2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1120" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1120</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1120</annotation></semantics></math> at inference time—see how this impacts quality in <a href="#S3.T5" title="In 3.4 Vision Token Budgets ‣ 3 Ablation Studies ‣ EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>. These soft tokens are then projected by the vision adapter and wrapped with delimiter tokens: <math id="S2.I1.i2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{T}_{\text{vis}}=\texttt{&lt;|SOI|&gt;}\oplus\phi_{\text{vis}}(\mathbf{T}^{\prime}_{\text{vis}})\oplus\texttt{&lt;|EOI|&gt;}\in\mathbb{R}^{(N_{\text{vis}}+2)\times d_{M}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐓</mi><mtext>vis</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">&lt;|SOI|&gt;</mtext><mo>⊕</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mtext>vis</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐓</mi><mtext>vis</mtext><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>⊕</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">&lt;|EOI|&gt;</mtext></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mtext>vis</mtext></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>M</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{T}_{\text{vis}}=\texttt{&lt;|SOI|&gt;}\oplus\phi_{\text{vis}}(\mathbf{T}^{\prime}_{\text{vis}})\oplus\texttt{&lt;|EOI|&gt;}\in\mathbb{R}^{(N_{\text{vis}}+2)\times d_{M}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S2.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;padding-top:5.0pt;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="S2.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Audio</span> is processed in 40ms chunks with Mel filterbank inputs, producing 25 soft tokens per second of audio: <math id="S2.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{T}^{\prime}_{\text{aud}}=\mathcal{A}(s_{m})\in\mathbb{R}^{N_{\text{aud}}\times d_{A}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐓</mi><mtext>aud</mtext><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mtext>aud</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{T}^{\prime}_{\text{aud}}=\mathcal{A}(s_{m})\in\mathbb{R}^{N_{\text{aud}}\times d_{A}}</annotation></semantics></math>. These are projected by the audio adapter and wrapped with different delimiter tokens to produce: <math id="S2.I1.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{T}_{\text{aud}}=\texttt{&lt;|SOA|&gt;}\oplus\phi_{\text{aud}}(\mathbf{T}^{\prime}_{\text{aud}})\oplus\texttt{&lt;|EOA|&gt;}\in\mathbb{R}^{(N_{\text{aud}}+2)\times d_{M}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐓</mi><mtext>aud</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">&lt;|SOA|&gt;</mtext><mo>⊕</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mtext>aud</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐓</mi><mtext>aud</mtext><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>⊕</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">&lt;|EOA|&gt;</mtext></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mtext>aud</mtext></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>M</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{T}_{\text{aud}}=\texttt{&lt;|SOA|&gt;}\oplus\phi_{\text{aud}}(\mathbf{T}^{\prime}_{\text{aud}})\oplus\texttt{&lt;|EOA|&gt;}\in\mathbb{R}^{(N_{\text{aud}}+2)\times d_{M}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S2.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;padding-top:5.0pt;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="S2.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Video</span> clips are typically sampled at 1 frame per second to begin. Then, for longer videos, frames are further sampled to fit a per-video frame budget <math id="S2.I1.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{\text{frm}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mtext>frm</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{\text{frm}}</annotation></semantics></math>—this is sometimes via truncation, by selecting the first <math id="S2.I1.i4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{\text{frm}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mtext>frm</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{\text{frm}}</annotation></semantics></math> frames, and sometimes via uniform sampling, by selecting <math id="S2.I1.i4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{\text{frm}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mtext>frm</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{\text{frm}}</annotation></semantics></math> evenly spaced frames over the entire video. During our training and evaluations we use <math id="S2.I1.i4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{\text{frm}}=32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mtext>frm</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{\text{frm}}=32</annotation></semantics></math>. Since each frame is processed by the vision encoder as an image, this results in up to <math id="S2.I1.i4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{\text{frm}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mtext>frm</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{\text{frm}}</annotation></semantics></math> segments, each with at most <math id="S2.I1.i4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{\text{vis}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mtext>vis</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{\text{vis}}</annotation></semantics></math> soft tokens and two image delimiter tokens.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.I1.i4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.I1.i4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Optionally, frames can be interleaved with audio tokens from the video’s soundtrack, with each frame coming first and then the audio that follows it divided into 1-second segments. Usually, this corresponds to a single 1-second audio segment per frame, but if frames are truncated we might have multiple trailing audio segments, and if frames are uniformly sampled, we might have multiple audio segments between frames. In interleaved video-audio, we include text timestamps in <span id="S2.I1.i4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MM:SS</span> format both before each frame and before each audio segment, to indicate when the frame is taken and when the audio chunk begins. Thus, video is represented as a combination of the former modalities, yielding an embedding sequence <math id="S2.I1.i4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{T}_{\text{vid}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐓</mi><mtext>vid</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{T}_{\text{vid}}</annotation></semantics></math> composed of interleaved sequences of <math id="S2.I1.i4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{T}_{\text{txt}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐓</mi><mtext>txt</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{T}_{\text{txt}}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S2.I1.i4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{T}_{\text{vis}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐓</mi><mtext>vis</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{T}_{\text{vis}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S2.I1.i4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{T}_{\text{aud}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐓</mi><mtext>aud</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{T}_{\text{aud}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Then, denoting as <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{T}_{m}\in\{\mathbf{T}_{\text{txt}},\mathbf{T}_{\text{vis}},\mathbf{T}_{\text{aud}},\mathbf{T}_{\text{vid}}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐓</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐓</mi><mtext>txt</mtext></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐓</mi><mtext>vis</mtext></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐓</mi><mtext>aud</mtext></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐓</mi><mtext>vid</mtext></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{T}_{m}\in\{\mathbf{T}_{\text{txt}},\mathbf{T}_{\text{vis}},\mathbf{T}_{\text{aud}},\mathbf{T}_{\text{vid}}\}</annotation></semantics></math> the embedding sequence of segment <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{m}</annotation></semantics></math>, the final concatenated sequence is <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{T}(x)=\texttt{&lt;|BOS|&gt;}\oplus\mathbf{T}_{1}\oplus\mathbf{T}_{2}\oplus\dots\oplus\mathbf{T}_{M}\oplus\texttt{&lt;|EOS|&gt;}\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times d_{M}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒯</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">&lt;|BOS|&gt;</mtext><mo>⊕</mo><msub><mi>𝐓</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>⊕</mo><msub><mi>𝐓</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>⊕</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">⋯</mi><mo>⊕</mo><msub><mi>𝐓</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><mo>⊕</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">&lt;|EOS|&gt;</mtext></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>M</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{T}(x)=\texttt{&lt;|BOS|&gt;}\oplus\mathbf{T}_{1}\oplus\mathbf{T}_{2}\oplus\dots\oplus\mathbf{T}_{M}\oplus\texttt{&lt;|EOS|&gt;}\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times d_{M}}</annotation></semantics></math>, with a total sequence length <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> of up to <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8192" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8192</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8192</annotation></semantics></math> during training. This is consumed by the model as <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{T}_{\text{in}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐓</mi><mtext>in</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{T}_{\text{in}}</annotation></semantics></math> in <a href="#S2.SS1" title="2.1 Architecture ‣ 2 EmbeddingGemma 2 ‣ EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Each training example includes multiple inputs: a query <math id="S2.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, a positive target (or <span id="S2.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">passage</span>) <math id="S2.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{i}^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{i}^{+}</annotation></semantics></math>, and (optionally) hard negative targets <math id="S2.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{p_{i}^{-}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{p_{i}^{-}\}</annotation></semantics></math>. An example may also include prescribed task prefixes <math id="S2.SS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{q}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.SS2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{p}</annotation></semantics></math> for queries and targets respectively, describing the nature of the task (see <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Task Instructions ‣ EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>). For instance, for retrieval we use “<span id="S2.SS2.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">task: search result | query:</span> {text}” and “<span id="S2.SS2.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">title:</span> {title | ‘none’} <span id="S2.SS2.p3.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">| text:</span> {text}”. The query and targets are embedded as vectors in <math id="S2.SS2.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S2.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{q}_{i}=f(\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{M}_{n}(\mathcal{T}(t_{q}\oplus q_{i})))),\quad\mathbf{p}_{i}^{\pm}=f(\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{M}_{n}(\mathcal{T}(t_{p}\oplus p_{i}^{\pm}))))." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐪</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒯</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>⊕</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐩</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>±</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒯</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>⊕</mo><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>±</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{q}_{i}=f(\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{M}_{n}(\mathcal{T}(t_{q}\oplus q_{i})))),\quad\mathbf{p}_{i}^{\pm}=f(\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{M}_{n}(\mathcal{T}(t_{p}\oplus p_{i}^{\pm})))).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.3 </span>Objective</h3>

<div id="S2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">EmbeddingGemma 2 was trained using multiple losses. Here we introduce the loss functions themselves, and in <a href="#S2.SS4" title="2.4 Recipe ‣ 2 EmbeddingGemma 2 ‣ EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.4</span></a> we explain how they are introduced during training.</p>
</div>
<section id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Contrastive loss</h4>

<div id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The first is a noise-contrastive estimation (NCE) loss with in-batch, hard, and same-tower negatives. Given a batch of size <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math>, we define the contrastive loss as:</p>
